messages.subject: How to do automatical-plotting
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am new to R and programming.

I have a large dataframe composed of two grouping variables (species, population, with populations nested in species) and tens of continuously numeric variables. For each numeric variable, I want to make a boxplot with population as the X axis and the boxes filled according to which species it is belonging to. But, that is a definitely tedious work. I followed the tutorials in the ggplot2 website. But, I have not found any way to ease this work.

I am really thirsting for an automatic approach to plot the numeric variables one by one in a PDF file, assigning the variable name as the y label. Can anyone share any brilliant scripts with me. I think it must be helpful to others who have little programming experience like me.

the code I used to make boxplot on (dataframe: All, group variable: species and popluation, and numeric variable: conlen) is as followed:

pcon<-ggplot(All, aes(population,conlen))
pcon+geom_boxplot(aes(fill=species))

Thank you in advance.

Regards
Mao J-F

On Mon, Jun 15, 2009 at 04:40:49PM +0800, Mao Jianfeng wrote:
> Hi everybody,
>
> I am new to R and programming.
>
> I have a large dataframe composed of two grouping variables (species,
> population, with populations nested in species) and tens of continuously
> numeric variables. For each numeric variable, I want to make a boxplot with
> population as the X axis and the boxes filled according to which species it
> is belonging to. But, that is a definitely tedious work. I followed the
> tutorials in the ggplot2 website. But, I have not found any way to ease this
> work.

I think there must be an easier way, but this one works also:

d = read.table("/tmp/da", header=T)

plotit = function(d, name){
p <- ggplot(d) + geom_boxplot(aes(x=population, fill=species, y=value)) + scale_y_continuous(name)
print(p)
}

pdf("/tmp/1.pdf")
for (i in 3:8){
data = d[,c(1,2,i)]
names(data) = c("species", "population", "value")
plotit(data, names(d)[i])
}
dev.off()

regards,
stefan

Try this,

# d <- read.table(pipe("pbpaste"), head=T) # read your data

str(d)
names(d)
# [1] "species" "population" "conlen" "tscale" "fscale"
#"tseen" "w100s" "nfsee"


variables <- setdiff(names(d), c("species", "population")) # remove
# x-axis and grouping variables


plotOne <- function(d, name="conlen"){
p <- ggplot(d, aes_string(x="population", y=name))+
geom_boxplot(aes_string(fill="species"))
print(p)
}

# plotOne(d)
# plotOne(d, "tscale") # works fine


# loop
library(plyr)

pdf("all.pdf")
l_ply( # list input, side-effect only
variables, plotOne, d=d)
dev.off()


I'm glad if it helped,

baptiste
